why: A (universes 0), for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V: curvR_of_mem (unfolding of the definition curvR); curvature_identity, (13.3) for ANY smooth surface F in N on an open O ⊆ ℝ² (P ∂_u(P ∂²_tF) = P ∂_t(P ∂_t∂_uF) + R(∂_tF, ∂_uF)∂_tF at p₀); IsVariation.hasDerivAt_jump, d/du Δ_x(∂α/∂t) = Δ_x(∂/∂t ∂α/∂u) for 1-parameter variations, as AMBIENT vectors (normal component included). B, for abstract connected ℝⁿ-manifolds with any Levi-Civita connection and 2-parameter variations (U ⊆ ℝ²): on open pieces D/∂u₁ of the accelerations at u = 0 is D²W₁/dt² + R(V,W₁)V (covariant derivative along r ↦ α(r e₀, s) on (-δ, δ)), and at interior break points D/∂u₁ Δ_tV = Δ_t(DW₁/dt). A ⇒ B fails genuinely (abstract manifolds). B ⇒ A fails genuinely: B is intrinsic, so it says nothing about the normal component of d/du Δ_x(∂α/∂t) contained in A's hasDerivAt_jump, and it gives (13.3) only for surfaces that are variations of paths (A's curvature_identity is for arbitrary local surfaces; recovering it from B would need cut-off/chart constructions of variations). curvR_of_mem is provable outright.
overlap: No A_to_B/B_to_A.
